title: Exploring Simple Siamese Representation Learning
layout_note: One input label 'image x' at the bottom centre splits through a bracket-like rounded line into two upward columns (x1 left, x2 right); the left column stacks encoder f then predictor h, the right column has encoder f only; both columns' lines bend inward at the top and meet at a single word 'similarity'.
grouping: No containers. The two branches are mirror columns; the shared encoder is shown by giving both columns an identical light-blue box with the same label 'encoder f', and the extra component on one side (predictor h) is a differently coloured (light orange) box.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with no outline: light blue for the two encoders, light orange for the predictor. Thin grey arrows with filled grey heads; the input split is a rounded grey bracket line. Serif math italics for labels (x1, x2, f, h).
proposed_highlight: The method's two distinguishing pieces are made the only differences between the columns: the predictor is the only orange box (left column only), and stop-grad is a dashed grey downward arrow crossed with an 'x' and labelled 'stop-grad', placed beside the right column's output line.
lesson: Show a Siamese method's asymmetry by keeping both branches identical except for one differently tinted extra box on one side and a crossed dashed arrow labelled 'stop-grad' beside the other side's output.
notes: Remembered venue: CVPR 2021 (not printed on the arXiv PDF's first page); year = arXiv preprint year. Column-width figure, minimal: four boxes and one word as the objective.

arrangement.units: Two unframed vertical branch columns separated by whitespace, joined at the bottom by a rounded split line and at the top by the 'similarity' label.
arrangement.inputs_as: text label 'image x' only, no picture; views named x1, x2 as italic labels beside the column feet
arrangement.losses_at: top centre, as the bare word 'similarity' where both branch lines meet; no box
arrangement.shared: the shared encoder is drawn twice, once per branch, as identical light-blue boxes with the same label 'encoder f'

taxonomy.note: training tag: SimSiam has no EMA teacher; it predicts the stop-gradient output of its own other branch, the closest listed value is self-distillation

insights.structure: Two mirror columns rise from one input: the left holds encoder f plus a predictor h box, the right holds encoder f alone, and both lines converge at the top on a single 'similarity' word.
insights.data: Data are never drawn: the image and its two views are only italic labels (image x, x1, x2) at the column feet.
insights.emphasis: The predictor is the only orange box against two light-blue encoders, and stop-grad is a separate dashed arrow with an 'x' beside the right branch, so the two design choices are the only visual differences.
insights.flow: Reading runs bottom-to-top: the rounded split at the bottom forks into the columns, each goes straight up, and the tops bend inward with arrowheads pointing at 'similarity'.
insights.avoid: The stop-grad mark floats beside the right column instead of sitting on its output line, so which edge it cuts is inferred rather than shown.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
